$comment: #EXP-2138 (Danny, 2026-11-25): DELETING REMOVES THE TRANSCRIPT. What a device keeps of a chat (its run record, journal and diff sidecar, scratch dir, its rows of the chat store) is removed by deleting the chat, its agent or its team, and by nothing else here: ending, archiving, moving (device, Assistant, group chat) or trashing a board keeps it, and a row missing from sync or from a read never removes anything (a message cache of a chat the account may no longer read goes too, see `unreadable`; the other removers are the machine's `Keep session history` window and a deliberate sign-out of the chat store). SERVER: `sessions.heldGone {ids: uuid[] (at most limits.batch)}` (POST) -> `{gone: uuid[], unreadable: uuid[]}`, a person's login only (an `expu_` key, an MCP call or an agent gets FORBIDDEN). heldAnswer(row, caller): an id is KEPT when its row exists and the caller STARTED it (no membership needed), or is a member of its team and it is `shared`, or OWNS a device row of the machine the row names (whoever may read it: a shared box runs teammates' private chats). Else `gone` = the row does NOT exist (deleted), `unreadable` = it exists and the caller may not have it (a left team, `shared` off, a move off the caller's machine, a changed or deleted devices row: no deletion). So the caller learns that an id still exists; only for ids it already holds (random UUIDs, a person's login, limits.batch per call). `serverCases`. THE SIGNAL: the delete itself (`sessions.delete`, `agents.delete`, `teams.delete`, the admin's and the import sweep's team delete) sends every session of the deleted trees, live or not, `kill {sessionId, reason: "deleted"}` down its device's control socket, after the commit, the targets read before it. An older relay or client drops `reason` (an ordinary kill). DEVICE (desktop app and CLI daemon), per account (its id names the instance and the user, so another login never shares state): candidates = the session ids of the account's run records (repo-backed too; a `/btw` aside is no session of the server) and of its chat store (a root's own rows carry its id), uuids only (`candidateCases`). It asks once signed in and synced, then every limits.askEveryHours; a notice asks at once, for the noticed ids only. heldPass({now (ms), holds, cached (the ids the chat store names), asked, answer {gone, unreadable} (null = the whole ask failed, was refused or did not parse, both fields required: nothing changes), state {id: {kind, first, last}}, notices}) -> {remove, uncache, state, notices, capped}: an asked id answered neither loses its first answer and its notice; an unreadable one loses its notice (it was not deleted) and, when not cached, its first answer (nothing to remove); an id in both lists is unreadable; a gone one with a notice is removed at once; any other one stores its kind and the answer's time (`first`, `last`) durably and is removed by an answer at least limits.confirmHours after `first`; `now` before `last` (the clock went backwards) or the other kind starts over. A gone id goes to `remove`, an unreadable one to `uncache`. A notice alone removes nothing. Only asked ids count. CAP: more than limits.capCount removals, both kinds together (noticed ids exempt), that are more than half of `holds` remove nothing but the noticed ones; the first answers stay. State and notices of ids no longer held are dropped; a removed id keeps its entry until its files are really gone (the host clears it). A run live here is ended first; while it lives nothing of it is removed (the next pass tries again). `passCases`. UNCACHED: the chat store's messages, events, docs and tools of the session, nothing else: the run record, journal + sidecar and scratch dir of a run this device hosted stay. A journal whose session is not synced is not taken into the chat store again. REMOVED (`removeCases`): this account's run record, its scratch dir (only when no other record names it; a repo worktree is never touched), the journal + diff sidecar when the record is this account's, or when no record names it, this account's chat store does and no other account's on this machine does; the chat store's messages, events, docs and tools of the session. A journal no account can be tied to stays. Mirrors: TS src/held-gone.ts, desktop `domain::held_gone` (host half `steer::held_gone`); the phones and the web hold no run records.
